servicePara: The steps are read beside the screenshots, because every instruction the article gives is read against the screen it says the reader will see. An article read top to bottom sounds clear; it does not find the button the text calls “Save” that the screenshot labels “Apply”, or the step that only works if a setting three articles away was turned on first.

seo.home: One help article read the way the customer who is stuck halfway through a task reads it: the title checked against the question it answers, prerequisites checked for being stated before step one, every step checked against the labels in the screenshots supplied, and the end checked for telling the reader what success looks like. One payment, no subscription.
seo.services: The help article review, priced per article, in twenty-four steps. No technical writing, no product testing, no support, nothing rewritten, no packages and no retainer.
seo.service: Send one help article with its screenshots. The title checked against the question, prerequisites checked for being up front, every step checked for one action and for the labels its screenshot shows, and the ending checked for a visible result and what to do if it does not appear.
seo.pricing: One rate per article at $49.99, in twenty-four steps from $49.99 to $1,199.76. No packages, no subscription, no volume discount and no surcharge.
seo.howItWorks: Write the brief with who reads the article and what they are trying to do, attach the article and its screenshots, pay in a panel on the same page, and get findings step by step back in three business days.
seo.standards: What Help Article does not do: no technical writing, no use or testing of the product, no customer support, nothing certified, and nothing rewritten.
seo.about: A help article is not documentation for its own sake but the one page a stuck customer reads before they give up or open a ticket, and Help Article reads one the way they do: step against screen.
seo.faq: Why the review does not test the product, why an article written by the engineer who built the feature is still worth checking, why nothing is rewritten, what makes customers give up, and what to send with the article.
seo.resources: Notes on why the title has to be the customer’s question, why prerequisites go before step one, why a step has to use the label on the screen, and why an article has to say what success looks like.
